varieties.name: Electra
varieties.traits: Tolerant to late blight (Phytophthora infestans); highest and most consistent yielder of the seven cultivars trialled over four seasons; oval/round tuber, yellow skin, yellow flesh; season length 150 days planting-to-harvest
varieties.note: KZN DARD's Cedara trial names this the top all-round pick, explicitly recommended for both commercial high-rainfall production and resource-poor smallholders.

evidence.quote: In the 2017/18, 2018/19 and 2019/20 seasons, and overall, Electra produced significantly higher yields than the other cultivars.
evidence.doc: Potato cultivar evaluation at Cedara, KZN DARD Research & Technology Bulletin 2021/22-02

evidence.quote: Electra, Valor and Panamera have good tolerance to late blight. Therefore, these three cultivars will be better suited for resource-poor smallholder and household growers.
evidence.doc: Potato cultivar evaluation at Cedara, KZN DARD Research & Technology Bulletin 2021/22-02

evidence.quote: Commercial potato producers should produce cultivars that the market wants. However, as Electra yielded consistently well, all producers in the high potential rainfall areas of KwaZulu-Natal should consider producing and marketing this cultivar more extensively, because of its high yield potential
evidence.doc: Potato cultivar evaluation at Cedara, KZN DARD Research & Technology Bulletin 2021/22-02

evidence.quote: The main cultivars grown in the province are Mondial, Valor and Sifra (Potatoes SA, 2019).

midlands-mistbelt.text: Directly sourced (this trial ran at Cedara, in the KZN Midlands): favour Electra, Valor or Panamera for their late-blight tolerance if growing without a full fungicide programme; Electra gave the highest, most consistent yield of the seven trialled.

highveld.text: The Cedara trial's cultivars (bred for the cool, higher-rainfall interior) are extrapolated here to the wider hard-frost interior, not independently confirmed for the highveld itself — treat as a reasonable but unverified extension of the KZN Midlands result.

gaps: All seven cultivars and their agronomic data come from a single KZN Midlands (Cedara) trial; no independent source confirms performance in the highveld proper, so that zone assignment is an inference, not a direct citation.

No sourced recommendation at all for lowveld-bushveld, subtropical-coast, western-cape, southern-cape, karoo-arid or high-mountain — Potatoes SA's region-by-region cultivar guide (referenced within the KZN DARD bulletin as 'Potatoes SA, 2019') was not itself locatable/fetchable this session.

No spacing, seed rate or yield-in-t/ha figures sourced for any cultivar; the bulletin reports only relative yield rankings (via letter groupings on a chart), not absolute t/ha numbers in extractable text.
